content.title: About
content.content: Raspberries are the edible berries of the Rubus idaeus shrub. Fresh raspberries are bright red, sweet‑tart, and have a delicate, slightly fragile texture. They are harvested in season (June‑August) and enjoyed fresh or used in cooking, baking, desserts, juices, and jams.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Raspberries belong to the rose family and are closely related to blackberries and blueberries.
Each berry is composed of many small drupelets, each containing a seed.
Fresh raspberries provide over 30 mg of vitamin C per 100 g, making them an excellent source of this vitamin.
They are rich in antioxidants, especially anthocyanins, which give the fruit its vivid color.
In ancient Roman medicine, raspberries were used as a remedy for colds and digestive complaints.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, aids collagen synthesis, and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, helps maintain satiety, and assists in blood‑sugar regulation.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and quercetin protect cells from oxidative stress and may lower the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Flavonoids in raspberries improve vessel function and can help reduce blood pressure.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: 100 g of fresh raspberries contain about 52 kcal, making them suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to raspberries, ranging from skin rash to swelling or breathing difficulties.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Raspberries are often treated with pesticides; thorough washing before consumption is recommended.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity may irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcer disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raspberries can be eaten fresh, added to yogurt, oatmeal, smoothies, salads, baked goods, and desserts. They can be made into jam, sauces, or cordial. For a longer shelf life, lightly dry them in the oven to create dried fruit.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh raspberries in the refrigerator in an airtight container, preferably on the middle shelf where temperature is stable. Consume within 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze the berries in a single layer on a tray, then transfer to a freezer bag.
